_note: The places of the site that Insight can lead to by the MEANING of a question (site 2.13, 17 November 2026; the senior author asked "how can i use test kits at home", was told "We haven't checked exactly this yet" although the site has a part on test kits to use at home, and wrote: "i should be answered and be given links etc and i think we already have info about that on the website. man we have to incorporate every instance of human language it is still stupid"). Until then a place was found only by patterns of words (site/src/app.insight.js, INS_PLACES, INS_RE): a wording nobody had foreseen found nothing. Here each place has the ways people ask for what it holds, in everyday words; the build turns them into the model's numbers (scripts/insight/build_index.py, places_index), and the page looks for the nearest way when no checked answer is a best match and no pattern gave the answer (insWhere). 'cut' and 'near': at 'cut' or more the place is the answer to what was asked (it is shown first, and nothing says "we haven't checked"); from 'near' to 'cut' it is a place to look, under the line for a question we have not checked. Both were measured (data/verification/insight/places-gold.json; scripts/insight/build_index.py --places). 'part': on a page of one drug, when the question names that one drug, the same part of that drug's page (d-kits, d-law, d-doses, d-looks, d-help) is where it leads. A way is written without a drug's name ("it" stands for the drug). A way must be a question the place really holds something on: a place is never offered for an answer it does not have. Adding a place or a way: measure again before it ships. 'topic' (site 2.22, 18 November 2026; the senior author asked, in six words that name no drug, whether one sex uses more than the other, and was shown the part "Are women and men different?" as if it were the answer, with nothing sent and nothing looked up, and wrote: "it think it knows but it does not"): a part of the Big questions page holds several answers on a subject; it is never THE answer to a question, however near. It is always a place to look, under the line that says the question is not answered yet, and the question is sent and looked up like any other. A question that names no drug and holds no drug word, but is nearest to such a part ('near' or more), is a question about drugs by its meaning: of the 165 questions about other things none comes that near to any place.
